**The 1861 round, Standard Hill to the Ropewalk.** Extra Parochial, Nottingham, schedules 72 to 133, read from the enumerator's page by A. Hagues. Nothing here is filed to a house: the pages give a street and almost never a number, and the numbering is not yet settled - see [[three-western-terrace-households-before-number-one]] for the same trouble on Western Terrace.

**Every page total checks.** Nine sheets, each adding to its own printed count of houses, males and females.

## People the later rounds have been waiting for

**Robert Henry Speed**, schedule 81, a solicitor of **28** keeping house on Park Terrace with two servants and no family. The record knows him as the Cavendish Road East solicitor of 1891, by then 68 with a son in the practice.

**John Maddock Perry**, schedule 91, merchant, with **John Thorpe Perry aged 1** and **William Thorpe Perry aged five weeks**. John Thorpe Perry is the retired solicitor the record has at **17 Cavendish Crescent North in 1939**, aged 79. Seventy-eight years, from a baby on Park Terrace to an old man in the crescent.

**Henry Wing**, schedule 93, attorney and solicitor, **30**, with his sister keeping house for him. The record holds two men of that name, both born 1831, and this is where they start.

**William W Lewis**, schedule 84, hosier, **32**, brother to James W Lewis and born like him at Tewkesbury. The record welds him to another William W Lewis - see [[two-william-w-lewises-welded-into-one]] - and a birthplace in Gloucestershire is the sort of thing that will tell them apart.

**William Archibald Patterson**, schedule 116, silk throwster **employing two hundred**, living with his father William Patterson, retired, and six grown brothers and sisters. The 1871 round has a William A Patterson on the Ropewalk whom the record could not place; the son is the likelier of the two.

**George Berrey**, schedule 114, lace manufacturer, on the Ropewalk. He is on Pelham Terrace in 1871 and at Linden House, Clumber Road, in 1881 - three streets in twenty years.

**Nathaniel Dickenson**, schedule 117, pawnbroker, with seven children. He is at 6 Western Terrace by 1871.

## And some who are simply worth having

**Charles Edward Burt**, schedule 104, a **Major of the Royal Artillery** of 29, with his gunner-servant Thomas Higgins, Higgins's wife and five Higgins children born at Woolwich, Portsmouth and Wakefield - a soldier's family, and a posting history written in birthplaces.

**William Henry Blackmer**, schedule 108, proprietor of houses, keeping a **boys' school** on the Ropewalk: three daughters and a boarder all working as governesses, and ten boys aged seven to eleven, two of them born in Australia.

**Sarah Wise**, schedule 131, schoolmistress, keeping a **girls' school**: two teachers, four scholars and two servants, with pupils born at Antwerp, Maryport and Brinsley.

**Moritz Jacoby** and **Edward Stegemann**, both lace merchants born in Germany, on the same street; **Jonathan Reckless**, lace manufacturer, with a wife born in France.

**Samuel Newham**, schedule 110, magistrate, 74. **Thomas Herbert**, schedule 112, lace manufacturer and magistrate. **Thomas Ball**, schedule 132, lace manufacturer and **town councillor**.

## Two names that matter to the rest of the record

**Knipton, Leicestershire** is here as a birthplace at schedule 129 - the form A. Hagues corrected the record to when the geocoder had it as Kimpton.

**James Roger Allen appears twice**, at 32 on Newcastle Terrace and at 67 on Western Terrace. They are two men and most likely father and son; the younger one's three boys are all born on Standard Hill.
